tasks.title: Finalise the entry ceiling: long PVC ceiling planks
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the entry ceiling will be PVC. Square 24 x 24 inch tiles were considered and dropped the same day: the entry is only about 1.0 m wide, so a 610 mm tile fits barely one and a half times across. Instead use LONG PVC ceiling planks (the interlocking strip type, commonly about 250 mm wide and sold in 3 m lengths), finalised after visiting some shops. Proposed: run them along the length of the entry (about 2.1 m), so each plank is one piece with no end joints and about four planks cover the width. Lights: ROUND recessed LED panel lights, the type already used in the home (Orient Electric 12 W recessed panel, 1,200 lumens), but single-colour, not the 3-in-1 colour-changing version; the owner confirmed again on 2026-10-04 that the entry gets a circular light, not linear ones. Proposed, not yet agreed by the owner: neutral white (4000 K), two lights of 6-8 W each along the length, on one switch at the door. Now drawn in the 3D model (Main entry and Whole home 3D, src/config/entryLightingConfig.js): two 8 W round panels (120 mm, 105 mm cut-out) on the centre line of the corridor, about 540 mm in from each end wall and 1.1 m apart; plus two surface-mounted round panels of the same family in the inner gallery (see the gallery note in task elec-entry-ceiling). The lights are drawn at the slab because the ceiling drop is not decided. Still to decide: the plank width, design and colour, the edge trim, the height the ceiling drops to, and whether anything above must stay reachable.

tasks.title: Drawing Room: finalise layered lighting with track lights (no false ceiling)
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04, decided: track lights plus the existing chandelier, no false ceiling, no table lamps and no swing-arm wall lights. The room has TWO ceiling fans (one at each end) and the chandelier midway between them. Drawn in the 3D model (Drawing Room, layout C): 48 V magnetic surface track, white, fixed straight to the slab. Track 1, 1.5 m, parallel to the TV wall and 540 mm from it (moved inboard of the ceiling moulding 2026-10-05): three 7 W spot heads (about 600 lumens each, 24-36 degree beam, anti-glare) aimed at the fluted panel, none at the screen. Track 2, 2.45 m (stops short of the corner ring), along the west wall 640 mm off it, over the sofas: two 15 W diffused linear heads (about 1,400 lumens each) between the two fans, and three 12 W READING heads (about 1,000 lumens each, 36 degree beam) pointing straight down at the seats: the two ends of the west sofa and the west end of the south sofa. Reading is done by turning Track 2 up; it is dimmed for TV. Totals: 3.95 m of track, 8 heads, 87 W, about 7,600 lumens, all dimmable. CIRCUITS (owner, later 2026-10-04): the heads on a track cannot be dimmed one by one, only the whole track, so ONE TRACK = ONE CIRCUIT, each with its own 48 V driver and its own wall dimmer: Track 1 on a 60 W driver (21 W of heads), Track 2 on a 100 W driver (66 W of heads), both hidden where they can be reached (the cap of the panel wall). Track 2 keeps its reading and diffused heads together on one dimmer: turn the whole track up to read, down for TV; the chandelier carries the general light. The mix of light on a track is fixed by which heads are clipped on. Colour: warm white 3000 K for the spots; the diffused and reading heads may be the tunable 3-in-1 type, neutral white being better for long reading. Mood light: dim the tracks, and use colour-changing (RGB + warm white) LED strip for the strip on top of the TV panel and the glow under the south sofa. Keep downward heads out from under the fan blades.

tasks.title: Sliding doors between the Drawing Room and the Lobby: aluminium frame, fluted glass, nothing on the floor
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04, decided: slim aluminium frame with fluted glass, and NOTHING on the floor. The opening is about 3,280 mm wide and about 2,395 mm high under the hanging beam (model sizes, not measured). How to build it: top-hung sliding panels, all the weight carried by a track fixed under the beam, no floor track. Three panels of about 1,100 mm on a three-line (telescopic) track, linked panel to panel at the bottom so they steady each other; the only guide is one small fitting at the parking end, beside the wall and out of the walking line. Proposed: extend the track about 1.1 m past the opening along the solid wall north of it, so the panels park in front of that wall and the whole opening is clear. Glass: 8 mm toughened, fluted (vertical flutes); if toughened fluted glass is hard to find locally, use clear toughened glass with a fluted film. Soft-close dampers; brush seals at the top and between panels and a brush strip along each bottom edge, to hold the AC cooling; recessed flush pulls. Each panel weighs roughly 55-60 kg, about 180 kg in all, hanging from the beam. PVC folding and crystal folding were considered and dropped. The 3D model still draws a 10-panel folding partition.
tasks.needs: Measure the opening width and the height under the beam; engineer or fabricator to confirm the beam takes about 180 kg on anchors; which side the panels park on (Drawing Room or Lobby face of the wall); frame colour
tasks.estimateBasis: opening 3277 x 2395: 84.5 sq ft x Rs 1,100-1,800. Model sizes (scan: about 3100 x 2445). Toughened fluted glass may not be stocked locally.

tasks.title: Drawing Room south window: roll-up sun screen on the outside (bamboo chick or ready-made HDPE blind, decided after the trial)
tasks.detail: Owner 2026-10-04: the window faces south-west and takes a lot of sun and heat in the Delhi summer; a curtain is used now. A roll-up screen (bamboo chick) on the outside stops the heat before it comes through the glass. New information from the owner: the top of the window, about 1 ft, is a FIXED band, and the opening shutters start below it; there is a cover above the window. Design (drawing: docs/drawings/south-window-chick-cord.png): hang the screen close to the wall, about 85 mm out, from hooks just under the frame head. Rolled UP, the roll (about 100 mm across) parks in front of the fixed band, above the shutters, so all six shutters open freely under it. Rolled DOWN, it covers the whole window; the shutters must be shut first, which they are on a hot afternoon with the AC on. The pull cord comes INTO the room through a small lined hole (brass or ceramic eyelet) in the frame head and ties on a hook inside, so it is worked from inside. Hook the bottom rail to two hooks at the sill when it is down, so wind cannot swing it. PHONE SCAN 2026-10-04: the frame is 2,700 wide, the drop from the head to the sill about 1,500 and the top band about 390. Owner 2026-10-05: a ready-made outdoor HDPE roll-up blind is being considered instead of bamboo, tried first on one section (see the trial task); a 3 ft (914) piece suits one section, and three 4 ft pieces do not fit side by side. Stainless steel hooks. Plain bamboo lasts two or three monsoons outside; a PVC-coated or HDPE outdoor screen looks similar and lasts longer. This replaces the earlier idea of hanging it 450 mm out from the edge of the cover: no long brackets, less wind sway, better shade.
tasks.needs: The result of the trial piece (OPEN_ITEMS C20). Measure the height of the fixed top band (the rolled screen must fit inside it) and the window width. Society rules on the outside look
tasks.estimateBasis: pieces: 2 to 3 each x Rs 800-1,800. After the trial piece; a made-to-measure bamboo chick is in the same range.
